title: UserGems vs. Vector: Which one is built for marketing-led ABM?
summary: Comparing UserGems vs. Vector? See how they differ on account scoring, contact-level ads, and pricing, and when marketing should run both together.
body_markdown:
Marketers shopping for contact-level ABM often end up comparing UserGems and Vector. Both can tell you who at your target accounts is showing interest. The difference is what your team can *do* with that signal.


UserGems is a sales command center that also does marketing. It turns that signal into outreach, with job-change alerts, AI-drafted emails, and sequences in Outreach, Salesloft, or Gong. When sales owns the next step, it does that job well.


Vector is an ABM platform built specifically for marketers. It shows who your ads reached and what that did for pipeline. You can hand sales a list of hot accounts with the evidence behind every one. Your audiences update themselves on the ad channels you already use. And when a deal opens, you can show which people your ads reached first.


If marketing owns ABM at your company, that’s the platform you need. The rest of this guide compares the two on scoring, ads, and price, and covers where each one is the stronger choice.


## How do UserGems and Vector work?


UserGems is an outbound and ABM platform centered on rep outreach. Vector is a contact-level ABM platform centered on marketing programs.


### UserGems


UserGems is best known for job-change tracking. When a past customer or champion moves to a new company, reps hear about it. It’s the core of the product, and UserGems’ data here is the category standard.


UserGems calls itself the “AI command center for outbound and ABM,” and outbound is where the product goes deepest. Its AI agent, Gem-E, builds lists and drafts outreach for email, phone, and LinkedIn. It then pushes buyers into sequences in tools like Outreach and Salesloft.


UserGems also offers marketing features, but they sit at the edges of the product. Outbound is the center, and the marketing pieces are built to feed it. Those include contact-level intent, website de-anonymization, account scoring, and audience sync to LinkedIn, Meta, and Google. Ads, intent, and de-anonymization start at its $75K Advanced tier. Its scoring is tuned to tell reps who to work next.


### Vector


Vector runs the whole ABM loop in one platform, and it starts with signals. Website visits, LinkedIn engagement, CRM activity, research intent, and job changes are each tied to a named person and the account they belong to.


Those signals feed[Specter (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/platform/scoring) , the scoring model that places each account in a buying stage. Specter explains in plain language why the account is there and who in the buying committee is in market. Contact-level audiences sync to your ad channels and refresh on their own, and sales gets alerts in Slack or your CRM. When a deal opens or closes,[Stories (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/platform/stories) turns that activity into a written record of who engaged and which ads and content reached them. Each step feeds the next, from the first signal to the closed deal.


## What’s the real difference between UserGems and Vector?


Both tools can pick up the same signal, and both can put that person in an ad audience. The difference is what the signal drives by default. In UserGems, it drives a rep’s outreach. In Vector, it moves the account to a new buying stage, and the audiences, alerts, and pipeline story all follow from that stage.


Take this signal: a VP of Finance at a target account reads your pricing page twice this week.


In UserGems, that’s a reason to reach out. Gem-E can add her to a list, draft an email and a call script, and drop her into a sequence. Gem-E can also add her to a LinkedIn, Meta, or Google audience automatically. The workflow is built around the rep’s follow-up, and when sales owns the next step, it’s a strong one.


In Vector, the same visit moves the account to a new buying stage, with the pricing-page activity listed as the reason. She lands in the audience built for that stage, so the ads she sees match where the account is. When the account moves to the next stage, her ads move with it. And if the account opens an opportunity, Stories records that she saw your ads before the opportunity opened.


Both workflows work. Which one fits depends on who owns the next step at your company, and who’ll run the tool day to day.


### Who owns the tool decides how it gets used


A pattern comes up again and again with teams running UserGems today. Sales keeps it for outbound and job-change alerts, often happily. Marketing often uses it only for LinkedIn audiences and builds its own account scoring elsewhere, feeding in UserGems signals.


That fits a product whose core workflows end in a rep’s outreach. Its review base points the same way. Most of UserGems’ roughly 146[G2 reviews (opens in a new tab)](https://www.g2.com/products/usergems/) come from AEs and BDRs, and the praise centers on warm leads from job changes.


### If you’re replacing 6sense or Demandbase


Leaving 6sense or Demandbase usually means moving from account-level data to contact-level data.


Account-level intent tells you Acme is researching.[Contact-level data (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/what-is-intent-data) tells you *who* at Acme. UserGems and Vector both work at the contact level, so the deciding question is which one fits the team that will own the program. If that’s marketing, start with[how Vector compares to 6sense (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/vs/6sense) .


## UserGems vs. Vector at a glance


UserGems wins on job changes and outbound sequencing. Vector wins on scoring you can explain, ad channels, ad efficiency, and proof for marketing.

## Which has account scoring you can show to sales?


The one that explains why an account is hot, in terms a rep can check. Scoring is where ABM programs lose sales’ trust. Marketing hands over a[list of hot accounts (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/your-abm-platform-says-the-account-is-hot-now-what) , a rep calls two of them and finds nothing, and after a couple of bad hand-offs the list stops getting opened.


Both tools use AI to score accounts and show the signals behind the score. Vector’s model, Specter, places each account in a buying stage and explains its reasoning in plain language, so a rep can see why an account is hot before acting on it. In Vector’s benchmarking across 174 companies, the top 10% of Specter-scored accounts held about half of the next month’s new deals.

Some marketing teams on UserGems keep its signals and build their own scoring model on top. Whichever way you lean, put one test to every vendor you evaluate. Ask them to pick an account their model calls hot and show you why. If the answer needs a data scientist, sales won’t use it.


## Which is better for contact-level ads?


Vector, on channel breadth and ad efficiency. Both tools can get a contact list into LinkedIn. What happens after that is where they split.


### More channels, audiences that keep up


UserGems includes audience sync to LinkedIn, Meta, and Google on its $75K Advanced tier and above. Vector runs contact-level audiences on LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Reddit, X, Bing, and ChatGPT.


Vector’s audiences also refresh themselves as buyers move between stages. The person who just read your pricing page sees a different message from the one who’s never heard of you, and nobody[rebuilds a list every week (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/always-on-audiences-the-b2b-ad-play-that-actually-works) to make that happen.


### Bids that adjust themselves


[Bid Agent (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/platform/advertising/bid-agent) rewrites your LinkedIn bids every 15 minutes.[When Fingerprint ran it (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/contact-level-abm-how-fingerprint-rebuilt-their-motion-and-opened-up-new-channels) across eight campaigns, cost per click fell roughly 3x on average. UserGems’ advertising features focus on building and syncing audiences. Bid Agent takes it one step further by managing what you pay to reach those audiences, so the same budget buys more clicks.


### Freshness matters for every audience


Signals decay. A job change spotted 18 months late is a miss, and a pricing-page visit from last quarter tells you little about this one. Ask every vendor how quickly[a new signal reaches an audience (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/abm-timing-window) , and test it on accounts you know.


## Should you use UserGems and Vector together?


For a lot of teams, yes. Sales keeps UserGems for champion tracking and outbound sequences. Marketing runs Vector for account selection, scoring, contact-level ads, and[pipeline proof (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/marketing-influenced-vs-sourced-pipeline) .


One prospect laid out the stack they were planning in almost those words.[Clay for custom signals (opens in a new tab)](https://www.vector.co/blog/clay-vs-vector-build-your-abm-system-or-get-it-built-in) , UserGems for champion tracking, and Vector for contact-level ads, marketing influence, account tracking, and website identification. Each tool gets the job it was built for.

If you’re already on UserGems, look at which jobs it owns today. If marketing uses it for one piece, like LinkedIn audiences, and rebuilds scoring elsewhere, you’re paying for a full platform and using one piece of it.


UserGems may be enough if:


-


Sales owns pipeline, and outbound is your main motion.


-


Job changes and champion tracking drive most of your pipeline.


-


You want AI-drafted outreach sequenced in Outreach, Salesloft, or Gong.


-


Marketing’s ad needs stop at LinkedIn, Meta, and Google audiences.


Vector is a fit if:


-


Marketing owns ABM and paid, and needs to show what it did for pipeline.


-


You want account stages that sales can check, with the evidence behind them.


-


You advertise beyond LinkedIn, or want bids that adjust themselves.


-


You want to see which named contacts marketing reached before each deal.


Vector doesn’t write or sequence outbound. If your team needs an AI SDR, UserGems is the stronger choice for that job.


### How to run a fair evaluation


Run both tools on your own records. Upload your closed-won, closed-lost, and open-opportunity contacts, plus your target and customer accounts, and see what each tool shows on people you already know. UserGems runs its proofs of concept this way. Vector will do the same.


Then ask four questions:


1. 1


**Can it explain a hot account?** Pick one and ask why it’s hot, in terms a rep would accept.


2. 2


**How fresh are the signals?** Check them against accounts where you know what happened.


3. 3


**What happens to price at renewal?** UserGems changed its pricing three times in August 2026, according to[PricingSaaS (opens in a new tab)](https://pricingsaas.com/companies/usergems/diffs/2026W35) . Ask every vendor what you’ll pay in year two.


4. 4


**Who will run it day to day?** Name the person. Then ask how much of their week it takes.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is Vector a UserGems alternative?


For marketing teams, yes. Vector covers what marketing usually needs from UserGems, including contact-level signals, account scoring, and ad audiences. It also runs ads on more channels, manages LinkedIn bids with Bid Agent, and writes up each deal with Stories. For sales teams that rely on AI-drafted outbound sequences, UserGems remains the better fit.


### Does UserGems do ABM?


Yes. UserGems offers account and contact scoring, contact-level intent, web de-anonymization, and ad audience sync to LinkedIn, Meta, and Google. Ads, intent, and de-anonymization are included from its $75,000 Advanced tier. Its ABM features lean toward sales prioritization and outbound.


### Does Vector do outbound sequencing?


No. Vector sends sales alerts with context to Slack, HubSpot, and Salesforce, and reps follow up in their own tools. Teams that need AI-written sequences often pair Vector with an outbound tool like UserGems.


### How much does UserGems cost?


As of November 2026, UserGems’ published annual pricing is $40,000 for Core, $75,000 for Advanced, and $150,000 for Elite, plus implementation fees of $3,000 to $10,000. Enterprise pricing is quoted, and there’s no free trial. Pricing changed three times in August 2026, so confirm current terms before you sign.


### Can you use UserGems and Vector together?


Yes. A common split puts sales on UserGems for champion tracking and outbound, and marketing on Vector for scoring, contact-level ads, and pipeline reporting.
